public_rationale: Primary studies establish growing benchmark overlap in web data and actual contamination in a modern training corpus. Those findings make the claim plausible. They do not establish how often successive systems were trained on benchmark material or benchmark-like synthetic data. Treating increasing contamination risk as a measured increase in the training practice would decide the result through an added interpretation.
limitations: The evidence establishes occurrence and increasing risk more clearly than increasing prevalence among systems.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In recent years, as the financial stakes of benchmark performance have increased, AI systems have been trained more often directly on benchmarks or on synthetic data closely resembling them.
conditions: as the financial stakes of benchmark performance have increased

our_interpretation: Recent years means the several years preceding publication, operationalized as 2020 through February 17, 2026.
More often means an increase in the prevalence of this training practice. Individual examples establish occurrence but do not establish an increase.
Training exposure can be deliberate or accidental; the claim does not require proof that every developer intentionally cheated.
The financial-stakes phrase describes accompanying circumstances. It does not, by itself, establish financial incentives as the cause.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence across time shows that systems increasingly trained on benchmark examples or closely resembling synthetic examples, alongside evidence of increasing commercial stakes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence across time shows that such training did not become more common, or that its prevalence declined.

evidence.explanation: The researchers find benchmark duplicates in Olmo3 training data and experimentally show that duplicate-based training can improve benchmark scores. A single model family and constructed training experiments do not establish an industry-wide increase over time.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A consistent comparison of dated model training datasets or disclosures showing whether benchmark-based training became more prevalent, plus evidence documenting the accompanying commercial stakes.
